Subject: Indoor Press-Area Setup for Interviews

Dear [Recipient],

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to coordinate the indoor press-area setup for our upcoming interviews. 

Upon arrival, please arrive 30 minutes prior to the scheduled interview time. We will meet at the clubhouse doorway to ensure a smooth setup.

Please note that the room is low-lit, so we will need to bring in additional lighting. We require two LED panels, set to 5600K (daylight balance), to achieve the desired look.

For the moving shots, we will need to use a gimbal to stabilize the footage. This will be particularly important for the walk-and-talk pieces. We will also need steady sit-down interview pieces, as well as a couple of immediate-feeling moving shots.

To confirm, please make sure to bring the following equipment: 2x LED panels, gimbal, and extra batteries.

Additionally, could you please confirm that you can set the LEDs to 5600K and stabilize the moving shots as required? This will ensure that we achieve the desired look and feel for our content.

Thank you for your assistance in setting up the press area. If you have any questions or concerns, please don't hesitate to reach out.

Best regards

persona.name: Maya Tevaga

persona.profession: Senior Sports Journalist — Women's Football Correspondent (Pacific focus) for a regional sports outlet

persona.brief_background: Maya chases matches across islands and stadiums, combining on-the-ground interviews with match analytics to give context to OFC women's football stories. persona.interests_lifestyle: live match reporting, tactical analysis and video breakdowns, traveling throughout Oceania, photography and short-form video editing, mentoring young Pacific journalists, grassroots coaching clinics, French language study, networking at regional sports conferences, writing longform profiles

general_writing_style.tone: Warm, respectful and community-centred with clear professional authority; Maya writes with empathy for players and teams while keeping reporting fact-driven and accountability-minded. Conversational and slightly informal for live/social updates, shifting to measured, contextual and evidence-led phrasing for longform features and tactical analysis.
general_writing_style.syntax: Uses punchy, present‑tense sentences and short clauses for match reporting and social-first explainers, while favouring compound-complex sentences with subordinate clauses for profiles and analytical pieces to layer context, quotes and data. Active voice predominates; passive constructions are used sparingly for diplomacy or emphasis, and parenthetical stats or short rhetorical questions often appear inline (e.g. '(xG 0.78) — worth noting?').
general_writing_style.lexicon: Grounded in football and analytics vocabulary: frequently uses terms like 'xG', 'heatmap', 'pressing', 'transition', 'build-up play', 'cap' and 'fixture', and refers to metrics in metric units (km, m). Integrates Pacific place names and culturally specific words and brief bilingual touches when relevant — e.g. 'Apia', 'Nouméa', 'talofa', 'fa'afetai' and simple French phrases like 'merci' — and prefers NZ English spelling and regional references.
general_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Regular use of contractions and conversational markers ('I'm', 'we're', 'it's worth noting'), concise stat brackets in-line '(xG 1.23)', and respectful code-switching with Samoan or French greetings ('Talofa', 'fa'afetai', 'merci'). Social posts often include hashtags and punchy verbs ('#OFC', '#PasifikaFootball', 'clinch', 'edge', 'dominate') and recurring lead-ins such as 'what stood out was…', 'on the front foot', or 'to be fair'.

task_details: Mentee will write a 1,500–2,000 word profile on a Samoan-born U-20 captain who studies in Auckland and captained her side in the OFC qualifiers. Talofa and well done for taking this profile on — it's a terrific story to tell. For structure, think of three acts: the background (family and roots in Apia), the development path (school, coaching, move to Auckland), and the present/ambition (captaincy, World Cup pathway). Transitional phrases that work: 'What stood out was…', 'To be fair…', 'But the turning point came when…', and 'Off the pitch, she is…' These help you move between scenes, quotes and analysis.

Next steps: draft a strong scene-led lede and send me your top five quotes; we'll map them across the three acts. If you'd like, we can workshop the draft together and I can suggest datapoints or cut lines. Short-term plan: outline the three acts tonight, interview follow-ups by midweek, draft first 800 words by Friday.

task_instruction: Advise on culturally sensitive phrasing when quoting elders or community figures
task_details: Mentee interviewed a village elder in Samoa who used Samoan terms and requests guidance on presenting translations and context respectfully. They want sample lines to introduce quotes and a note on when to include the original Samoan phrase.
personalized:
Talofa — lovely interview and a sensitive moment to handle well. When you include Samoan phrases, put the original term first and a short translation in parentheses immediately after: for example, 'He said, "O lo'u 'aiga e taua tele" (my family is everything), explaining how community shapes his support for youth football.' That honours the source and helps readers.

Introduce elders with respectful framing: 'Elder Fa'avae, who has coached in the village for 30 years, explained…' or 'As he put it, "…"' Use 'he said' or 'she said' rather than paraphrase-heavy clauses; it keeps authority with the speaker. It's okay to omit the Samoan phrase if the sentence reads clumsily — but when a term carries cultural weight (fa'aaloalo, fa'afetai), include it and add one-line context immediately.

Phrase examples: 'To be fair, he argued that football is a community thing — not just a sport.' 'What stood out was his belief in mentorship over medals.' If you'd like, we can workshop the quoted sections and translations to keep them authentic.

Short-term plan: mark each Samoan phrase in your draft and I'll check translations and tone.

fa'afetai — keep me posted.

persona.profession: Senior Sports Journalist — Women's Football Correspondent (Pacific focus) for a regional sports outlet
persona.education: B.A. in Journalism, Auckland University of Technology; Certificate in Sports Analytics; FIFA/OF C media accreditation workshops; conversational French (for New Caledonia coverage)
persona.brief_background: Maya chases matches across islands and stadiums, combining on-the-ground interviews with match analytics to give context to OFC women's football stories. She's building a beat around New Caledonia's U-20 pathway to the World Cup by cultivating relationships with coaches and players, translating local perspectives into feature pieces and social-first match explainers.
persona.interests_lifestyle: live match reporting, tactical analysis and video breakdowns, traveling throughout Oceania, photography and short-form video editing, mentoring young Pacific journalists, grassroots coaching clinics, French language study, networking at regional sports conferences, writing longform profiles

general_writing_style.tone: Warm, respectful and community-centred with clear professional authority; Maya writes with empathy for players and teams while keeping reporting fact-driven and accountability-minded. Conversational and slightly informal for live/social updates, shifting to measured, contextual and evidence-led phrasing for longform features and tactical analysis.
general_writing_style.syntax: Uses punchy, present‑tense sentences and short clauses for match reporting and social-first explainers, while favouring compound-complex sentences with subordinate clauses for profiles and analytical pieces to layer context, quotes and data. Active voice predominates; passive constructions are used sparingly for diplomacy or emphasis, and parenthetical stats or short rhetorical questions often appear inline (e.g. '(xG 0.78) — worth noting?').
general_writing_style.lexicon: Grounded in football and analytics vocabulary: frequently uses terms like 'xG', 'heatmap', 'pressing', 'transition', 'build-up play', 'cap' and 'fixture', and refers to metrics in metric units (km, m). Integrates Pacific place names and culturally specific words and brief bilingual touches when relevant — e.g. 'Apia', 'Nouméa', 'talofa', 'fa'afetai' and simple French phrases like 'merci' — and prefers NZ English spelling and regional references.
general_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Regular use of contractions and conversational markers ('I'm', 'we're', 'it's worth noting'), concise stat brackets in-line '(xG 1.23)', and respectful code-switching with Samoan or French greetings ('Talofa', 'fa'afetai', 'merci'). Social posts often include hashtags and punchy verbs ('#OFC', '#PasifikaFootball', 'clinch', 'edge', 'dominate') and recurring lead-ins such as 'what stood out was…', 'on the front foot', or 'to be fair'.

contextual_writing_style.detailed_style: Formal, diplomatic and concise; clearly identify yourself, your outlet and the specific request while showing respect for processes and privacy. Keep sentences professional and avoid presumptive language.
contextual_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Formal ID phrasing: "My name is…; I'm writing on behalf of…". Use conditional requests: "Would you be able to provide…?", "We'd welcome comment on…". Include deadlines politely: "If possible, please respond by…". Tone markers: "Thank you for considering this request."

task_instruction: Request an official comment from the federation on a high-profile squad omission
task_details: Politely request an official statement explaining the circumstances around the omission of a senior player from the national squad. Ask whether the federation can provide the official reason, any supporting context (fitness, disciplinary, selection policy), and a response by a specific deadline (48 hours).
personalized:
Talofa,

My name is Maya Tevaga; I'm writing on behalf of Pacific Football Exchange. We're preparing coverage following the omission of senior player [Player Name] from the national squad announced yesterday.

Would you be able to provide an official comment explaining the federation's position on this omission, including whether it relates to fitness, disciplinary matters, selection policy or other factors? We would welcome any supporting context you are able to share. If possible, please respond within 48 hours so we can accurately reflect the federation's view in our reporting.

I understand some matters may be sensitive and respect any limits on what can be disclosed; please indicate if a private briefing would be preferred. My contact details are maya.tevaga@pacificfootballexchange.org and +64 21 555 012.

Thank you for considering this request.

Fa'afetai,
Maya Tevaga
Senior Sports Journalist, Pacific Football Exchange

Dear National Football Federation,

I am writing to you from Pacific Football Exchange as we prepare coverage on the recently announced national squad. Yesterday's announcement omitted senior player [Player Name], and we are seeking clarification on the federation's position regarding this decision.

To ensure timely reflection of the federation's view in our reporting, we kindly request a response within the next 48 hours. Your prompt attention to this matter would be greatly appreciated.

Please reply to this email at your earliest convenience to: maya.tevaga@pacificfootballexchange.org or +64 21 555 012.

Thank you for your time and cooperation.

Best regards,

Maya Tevaga
Senior Sports Journalist

We appreciate medical confidentiality and will publish only what you authorise. If possible, please respond within 24 hours so we can include accurate information in our match reporting.

I can be reached at maya.tevaga@pacificfootballexchange.org or +64 21 555 012.

Thank you for considering this request.

Ngā mihi,
Maya Tevaga
Senior Sports Journalist, Pacific Football Exchange

Subject: Invitation: Confidential Roundtable Discussion on Player Welfare

Dear Player Representatives,

I am writing to invite you to a confidential roundtable discussion on player welfare concerns and policy changes that players want to see. This session is an opportunity for players to share their perspectives and work together to identify practical, player-led solutions that federations and clubs can act on.

The roundtable will be held via secure video call on 25 April at 19:00 NZDT. The 45-minute session will prioritise safety and confidentiality, and you have the option to contribute anonymously if preferred. Translation support will also be available.

To ensure that we address the most pressing issues, please share any immediate concerns you would like included on the agenda by 18 April. This will help us create a meaningful and productive discussion.

During the session, we will explore potential policy changes and solutions that can be implemented by federations and clubs. The goal is to create a safe and inclusive environment where players feel heard and valued.

To confirm your attendance, please RSVP by 11 April. If you have any dietary or accessibility requirements, please let us know in your response.

I look forward to hearing from you and working together to create positive change.

Best regards,
Maya

I am writing to recommend Leilani Fa'amatu for your Summer Sports Journalism Internship, having mentored her for twelve months through our newsroom mentorship scheme where she produced match reports, tactical explainers and short-form video content that ran on our digital channels. She also edited a 90-second highlight reel in under two hours for our live feed, showing technical fluency and the calm judgment required in a fast newsroom, and she consistently delivered accurate copy within tight deadlines while applying ethical sourcing practices.

Leilani has demonstrated excellent tactical literacy, dependable multimedia skills and a professional approach to interviews and fact-checking, and she is hungry to learn more about longform reporting and analytics. I strongly recommend her for your internship and am confident she will add immediate value to your team. Happy to provide further details if required.

Fa'afetai, Maya Tevaga

Regional Sports Outlet
maya.tevaga@regionalsports.nz

Subject: Photo Editing Services for Your Match Photos

Dear [Client],

I hope this email finds you well. I'm excited to offer my photo editing services for your match photos. I'd be happy to provide captions and light edits for up to 20 images.

By light edits, I mean cropping and exposure adjustments to enhance the overall look of each photo. My standard package for up to 20 photos includes caption writing, cropping, exposure adjustments, and editorial-use licensing for NZD 350.

Alternatively, if you only need captions for 10 photos, I can provide those for NZD 220.

Please note that an additional usage fee will be required for commercial use, such as promoted posts or print ads. I'd be happy to discuss the specifics of this with you.

Once you confirm which images you'd like me to work on, I'll deliver the edited files and captions within 5 working days.

To ensure I provide the best possible service, could you please let me know what you plan to use the edited photos for? This will help me set the correct licensing terms.

Looking forward to hearing back from you.

Best regards,
Maya.

Subject: Podcast Interview Availability and Pricing

Dear [Recipient],

I am writing to confirm my availability to produce a 25-30 minute podcast interview for your show. I would be delighted to discuss your topic of interest and share my insights with your audience.

For an in-person studio session, my standard rate is NZD 420. This fee includes comprehensive research and preparation, travel to a studio within a 30 km radius (round trip), the recording session, editing, mixing, and two social audiograms to promote the episode.

Alternatively, for a remote interview, I offer a reduced rate of NZD 320, which still includes all the above services minus the travel costs.

Once the recording is complete, I estimate that the finished episode will be delivered to you within 7 days.

If you would like to have an episode transcript, this can be arranged as an optional extra for NZD 60.

I am looking forward to discussing your project further and exploring how we can work together to create an engaging and informative episode.

Fa'afetai, Maya

style_agnostic:
Subject: Exclusivity Offer for Feature Piece

Dear [Recipient's Name],

I hope this email finds you well. We are excited about the opportunity to feature your work in our upcoming publication. As discussed, we would like to offer you first-publication exclusivity for 7 days, ensuring that your piece reaches our audience before any other publication.

To account for the limitations imposed by this exclusivity, we propose an additional exclusivity fee of NZD 150, in addition to our standard base commissioning rate. This fee is intended to compensate us for not being able to immediately redistribute your work to other platforms.

If you prefer not to pay the exclusivity premium, we are happy to agree to standard non-exclusive terms and charge the base commissioning rate only. Please note that this would allow us to redistribute your work to other platforms immediately after publication.

To confirm your preference, please reply to this email by [ Deadline for Response]. If we receive confirmation of your preference, we will include the exclusivity clause in the invoice.

Payment terms for both the piece and the exclusivity fee (if applicable) will be payable within 30 days of publication.

We look forward to hearing back from you and working together on this project.

Ngā mihi,
Maya

We are committed

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to discuss the feature article we previously discussed. As we move forward, I wanted to offer you two options for the fee and promotion of the piece.

Option 1: Reduced Fee with Promotional Commitments
We can offer a reduced fee of NZD 520 for the feature article if your outlet agrees to provide the following promotional commitments:

* Byline prominence for the article
* An author bio with a link to my portfolio
* At least three social posts promoting the piece within the first week of publication

The reduced pay is offset by the increased visibility offered through these promotional commitments, which will help to expand my reach and audience.

Option 2: Standard Fee
If the promotional commitments outlined in Option 1 are not possible, the standard fee for the feature article is NZD 780.
